_about: PRO batch 46: era 4, The Veteran (34-37), set 3.

scenarios.title: The Specialists' Reunion
scenarios.text: The specialists you came up with, a punter, two snappers and three holders, meet for a reunion dinner. Half of them have gray hair, and all of them have stories.

choices.label: Stay until the restaurant closes
choices.result: Until the restaurant closes and they put the chairs on the tables. The stories get better every hour, and nobody wants to leave.

choices.label: Make a toast to the ones who left early
choices.result: A toast to the specialists whose careers ended too early. The table goes quiet, and then someone tells the funniest story of the night.

choices.label: Plan the next one
choices.result: The next reunion, planned before dessert: same place, every two years. You make the group chat and name it something terrible.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Tape Library
scenarios.text: You go through old tape of yourself in the film room, years of it, and the young kicker on the screen looks like a different person: faster, stiffer, more afraid.

choices.label: Find what you lost
choices.result: What you lost, found in the old tape: a quickness in your first step. You work on it for a month and get some of it back.

choices.label: Find what you gained
choices.result: What you gained, noticed for the first time: calm, patience, a better plant. You show the young kickers the before and after.

choices.label: Watch it with {parent}
choices.result: The old tape, watched with {parent} on a visit. He remembers every kick and where he was sitting for each one.

scenarios.title: The Second Wind
scenarios.text: A month where everything feels easy again: your leg is loose, your timing is perfect, and you wake up before the alarm wanting to go to practice.

choices.label: Enjoy every day of it
choices.result: Every day, enjoyed on purpose, because you know these months are rare now. You laugh more at practice than you have in years.

choices.label: Write down what's different
choices.result: Everything that's different, written down: the sleep, the food, the warmup. When the hard months come back, you'll know what to try.

choices.label: Push while it lasts
choices.result: Harder while it lasts: extra long kicks, extra sessions. You bank everything you can before the body changes its mind.

scenarios.title: The Missed Kick Story
scenarios.text: A reporter writes a long story about the kicks you've missed, not the ones you made: every famous miss of your career, in order, with photos.

choices.label: Read it all
choices.result: Every word, read once, in the car. It hurts, and it's fair, and some of it you'd forgotten. You throw the paper away and go to practice.

choices.label: Call the reporter
choices.result: A call to the reporter, polite and curious. He's surprised, and the follow-up piece is about how you came back from each miss.

choices.label: Let your family read it for you
choices.result: {love_interest} reads it and tells you there's nothing in it you need. You believe them, and you never read it.

scenarios.title: The Age Joke
scenarios.text: Every broadcast now has a joke about your age: the graphics, the commentators, and a cartoon of you with a cane during the pregame show that your kids think is hilarious.

choices.label: Make the joke first
choices.result: The joke, made first, at your own locker, with a borrowed cane. It becomes the most-watched clip of the week, and the broadcasters run out of material.

choices.label: Answer with your leg
choices.result: No comment, ever. Your leg answers for you, and by November the jokes are about how you're still doing it.

choices.label: Let it roll off
choices.result: It rolls off, mostly, like water. Your kids think the cartoon is hilarious, and by midseason you've started to agree with them.

scenarios.title: The Cortisone Talk
scenarios.text: A doctor offers a cortisone shot to get your hip through the season: legal, common, effective. It would mask the pain, and you'd have to decide what the pain is telling you.

choices.label: Take the doctor's full advice
choices.result: The doctor's full advice, asked for and followed: rest first, the shot only if the rest fails. It doesn't come to that, and your hip lasts the season.

choices.label: Ask for a second opinion
choices.result: A second opinion, from a specialist who has seen a thousand kickers. She agrees with the first doctor, and explains why in a way you finally understand.

choices.label: Play through it without the shot
choices.result: No shot, and you play through it the hard way. The hip aches all season, and you trust what it tells you.

scenarios.title: The Last Big Endorsement
scenarios.text: A national sponsor offers what may be your last big deal: one season, a commercial, and a farewell campaign about longevity. The ads will have your face on every bus.

choices.label: Sign the farewell campaign
choices.result: Signed, with your face on every bus. The campaign is tasteful and kind, and strangers start telling you to keep going.

choices.label: Make it about the kids
choices.result: Your condition: half the campaign goes to your foundation's youth clinics. They agree, and the ads feature kids kicking instead of you.

choices.label: Turn it down
choices.result: No farewell campaign before you've actually decided to say farewell. The sponsor understands completely and leaves the door open for next year.

scenarios.title: The Long Snapper's Son
scenarios.text: The son of the long snapper you started your career with is now a long snapper himself, and he's just signed with your club. He snaps exactly like his father did.

choices.label: Tell him about his father
choices.result: Stories about his father, told in the specialists' room, the good ones and the funny ones. He calls his father that night, and his father calls you.

choices.label: Teach him the timing
choices.result: The timing, taught the way his father taught you: patiently, with too many jokes. By September the snaps are perfect.

choices.label: Feel very old about it
choices.result: A very long moment of feeling old, then a laugh. You send his father a photo of the two of you, captioned 'how?'

scenarios.title: The Veteran Minimum, Again
scenarios.text: Another season at the veteran minimum, the third in a row. The number is still more than most people make, and it's a long way from what you used to make.

choices.label: Be grateful out loud
choices.result: Grateful, out loud, at your locker and at home. A paycheck to kick a ball at your age is a gift, and saying it makes it feel like one.

choices.label: Tighten the budget
choices.result: A tighter budget, built with your advisor and your family. Nobody misses much, and the kids think the new rules are funny.

choices.label: Earn a raise
choices.result: A raise, earned the old way: the best season of your late career. Your agent has a reason to call the club in March.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Hall
scenarios.text: Your hometown's sports hall of fame inducts you, in the high school gym, with a plaque, a dinner and your peewee coach in the front row.

choices.label: Thank your peewee coach
choices.result: Your peewee coach, thanked by name in your speech, and asked to stand. He's eighty and cries, and so does the whole gym.

choices.label: Bring the high school kickers on stage
choices.result: The high school's kickers, called up on stage with you. You tell the gym they're next, and you mean it.

choices.label: Keep the speech short
choices.result: Brief words at the podium, then a long night of handshakes. You see people you haven't seen in twenty years, and it's wonderful.

scenarios.title: The Old Friend's Funeral
scenarios.text: A friend from your rookie class has died young, of a heart attack, at home. The funeral is on a Wednesday, and half your draft class flies in.

choices.label: Speak at the funeral
choices.result: Some words at the funeral, the funny ones and the true ones. His kids laugh at one story and will remember it, which is exactly what you wanted.

choices.label: Look after his family
choices.result: His family, looked after quietly: rides, meals, a fund for the kids. You call his wife every month that year.

choices.label: Get a full checkup
choices.result: A full checkup the next week, the first in years, at {love_interest}'s insistence. Everything is fine, and you sit in the car afterward for a long time.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Concussion Story
scenarios.text: A retired teammate goes public about his concussions: the headaches, the memory, the bad years. Reporters ask every current player what they think, starting with you.

choices.label: Stand with him publicly
choices.result: Publicly, with him: he's brave, and the league should listen. He calls you that night and can't finish his first sentence.

choices.label: Call him privately
choices.result: A private call, long and quiet, with no reporters anywhere. He says later that it was the one call that really mattered to him.

choices.label: Push the union for action
choices.result: The union, pushed for action at the next meeting, with his story as the reason. Two changes pass by spring.

scenarios.title: The Partner's Patience
scenarios.text: {love_interest} asks you for one thing this season: no surprises. No secret injuries, no late decisions, no contract news they hear from the radio first.

choices.label: Promise and keep it
choices.result: Promised, and kept, all season: every injury, every rumor, every call, shared at dinner. It's the calmest season your house has ever had.

choices.label: Set up a weekly check-in
choices.result: Sunday nights, after the kids are asleep, a weekly check-in with no phones. Some weeks it's five minutes; some weeks it's two hours.

choices.label: Ask for the same in return
choices.result: No surprises, both ways, you ask. {love_interest} laughs, and agrees, and tells you something they've been saving for a month.
